user.title: Connect to Bria
user.description:
Enter the IP address (or hostname) of the machine running Bria and the API port (default 9002).

- **Same machine as HA**: leave host as `cpclientapi.softphone.com`.
- **Different machine** (e.g. `192.168.1.50`): enter that machine's IP. The integration handles the TLS certificate correctly automatically.

After the first connection, open Bria → Notifications tab → **Allow Access**.

safety.title: Safety
safety.description: Limit what Home Assistant can make Bria do. Anyone who can run automations or scripts can use these services, so only allow what you need.

data.allow_app_control: Allow sign in, sign out and exit

data_description.dial_allow_pattern: Optional. When set, place_call, transfer_call and start_attended_transfer only accept numbers that fully match, for example `\+?1?\d{10}` or `1\d{2}|\+1555\d{7}`. Leave empty to allow any number.
data_description.allow_recording: Recordings are saved on the Bria computer. Recording laws vary; check that you may record calls before turning this on.
data_description.allow_app_control: Lets automations sign Bria out or close it. These services are also limited to Home Assistant administrators.

tls_verification_failed.title: Bria certificate could not be verified
tls_verification_failed.description:
Home Assistant could not verify the TLS certificate of Bria at {host}: {error}

The integration trusts Bria's certificate for cpclientapi.softphone.com through its RapidSSL intermediate. If this fails, Bria's certificate has probably expired or changed issuer; updating Bria and this integration usually fixes it. As a last resort, reconfigure the integration and turn off certificate verification, but only if TCP port 9002 on that machine is firewalled to Home Assistant's addresses.
